strings.help.codex:
Recommended

Configuring .env lets Codex conversations use a proxy without enabling the system proxy, even when ChatGPT is opened without this launcher. It does not affect Chat. The protocol, address and port below will be written to .env.

This may help with Codex getting stuck at "Reconnecting (5/5)":
Codex normally tries WebSocket first. In some environments it may not use the system proxy correctly, then fall back to a different connection after retries. Setting .env can let the WebSocket connection use your proxy.

An unstable proxy can also cause repeated reconnections.

Save your work first. After saving .env, this tool will try to quit the entire ChatGPT desktop app. Reopen it to apply the Codex settings.
strings.help.protocol: Do not change this unless you know what you are doing.
strings.help.port:
Keep your usual proxy app running in the background. Click the empty port field to try automatic detection, then check that the detected port is correct.
If detection fails or finds the wrong port, open your proxy app settings, find its port settings, and enter that number here.

The launcher, launch options and sign-in startup shortcut have been saved. You do not need to deploy again.

Next steps:
1. Click OK to open Windows Startup apps settings.
2. Find ChatGPT and make sure it is Off. If it is already off, leave it as it is.
3. Keep ChatGPT Launcher (this tool’s startup entry) enabled.
4. Return to this tool and click Done.

This prevents ChatGPT’s own startup entry from running first and bypassing your launch options.
